title: Thunder Substack (by Andreea Popa): We develop leadership by learning to lead ourselves
summary: Andreea Popa profiles Manu, a Thunder team member who runs marathons and Spartan races, and argues that leadership grows from practicing self-leadership, not from holding a title. She draws lessons from Manu's answers: keep a plan, push a little further, lift others, believe in yourself, and treat every finish line as a start. The post does not report anything Cris said or did.

principles.text: Leadership is developed by practicing self-leadership, not by holding a title.
principles.quote: We develop leadership not by holding a title, but by practicing the activities that teach us to lead ourselves.

principles.text: Commit to a plan and keep it whatever the conditions; consistency removes excuses.
principles.quote: if I’ve scheduled four runs in a week, I complete them.

principles.text: You can usually go a little further than you think; a small push is often enough.
principles.quote: when you feel like you can’t, you actually can go a little more.

principles.text: Real strength lies in lifting others and sharing a common goal rather than competing.
principles.quote: Nobody competes against each other; we all share the same goal: to finish the race together.

principles.text: Treat each achievement as the start of the next challenge, an infinite mindset that avoids post-goal lows.
principles.quote: There’s no finish line for ambition. Every goal you reach is just the beginning of the next challenge.

principles.text: Discipline becomes freedom, and quiet, lasting leadership comes from steady repeated action.
principles.quote: These are the steps that turn discipline into freedom and action into quiet, lasting leadership.
